bluf: KlientBoost is a US paid media specialist selling itself as an outcome marketing agency with aggressive accountability, goal pacing and a free marketing plan as the door, claiming an average 63% ROI lift within the first three months. Paid search leads: the PPC page claims 250+ clients and $50M+ yearly ad spend, and it runs 49 Google ads and 23+ LinkedIn ads of its own. The record holds no moves, news or jobs. A rival should know that it sells paid social with no social pixel and CRO with no testing tool on its own house, and that all 10 clients on record are names without described work.
doing:
KlientBoost positions as an outcome marketing agency promising aggressive accountability and goal pacing, led by a free marketing plan: it buys ads for a mixed book and adds resources free when pacing behind goals. Its headline claim is an average 63% lift in client ROI within the first three months, a claim with no case study text behind it.

The sold mix leads with paid search, scored 3: the services index says paid ads built its reputation and the PPC page claims 250+ clients and $50M+ yearly ad spend. Five core lines score 2. B2B & ABM rests on a LinkedIn Ads page built for B2B demand generation and SaaS client cases. CRO rests on a landing page agency and design pages and CRO case studies for Brydge and Decked. Data & Measurement rests on the homepage Growth Grid. Paid Social rests on Facebook Ads and LinkedIn Ads pages. SEO rests on an SEO agency page, link building and content, and a GEO page. AI search, content, email and retail media score 1 with no evidence note; AI automation, creator, local, programmatic and web score 0. Proprietary lines are the Growth Grid, Free Marketing Plan 2.0 and marketing recipes (10+ custom playbooks); the record lists no partner badges.

Its AI posture cuts both ways: it sells a GEO service for AI recommendations while branding itself against AI hype, telling LinkedIn prospects it rejects AI powered everything shortcuts. The record lists no dated moves, news, case study text or jobs. Pricing signals: a pricing page in the main navigation and a free marketing plan billed as worth $10,000, though the Horus P5 read still finds no public pricing model. The record also holds claims of 200+ published case studies, 600 to 750+ five star reviews and a 2022 Glassdoor award. Conspicuously absent: an office list, ownership, headcount, partner accreditation, and any tag stack on its own site.
clients:
The record reads the client type as mixed and lists eight verticals: B2B & SaaS, ecommerce, fintech and payments, legal, healthcare, education, automotive and consumer robotics; the home market is the US, with no office list. The needs read holds 10 clients, 0 with an observed need and 10 named only, from 1 case study and 9 case study slugs. UBTECH Robotics is the one case study, with nothing about the work recorded. The slug only names are Salesloft, Druva, Delphix, Pushpay, Truckstop, Double Good, Shift4Shop, Method Race Wheels and Prodigy Education, needs inferred from the sold mix: paid performance for all, B2B pipeline for the SaaS names the LinkedIn Ads page speaks to, and commerce for the ecommerce names. The CRO capability note adds Brydge and Decked as CRO case studies outside the client list. Set against a claim of 200+ published case studies and 250+ clients, a record of 10 names and one case study page is the finding: the volume is asserted, the work is not shown.

One client is shared: UBTECH Robotics also sits on the book of valtech.

What the base needs next: the mixed book sits under KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out), the judgment the Horus read marks KlientBoost most exposed to through paid search, paid social and SEO, and KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), the one it is best placed for. It is likely, moderate confidence, that the SaaS and ecommerce accounts will keep buying the goal pacing story while the platforms take the buying hours, and likely, low confidence, that they will ask the GEO service for a measured number it does not yet show.
house: Say and do: five lines tested, three practised, integrity 60. Paid search is corroborated: it runs its own Google ads, 49 in the Transparency Center and 39 in the last 30 days, last shown 2026-09-21; one sample promises to make competitors 'Cry Like Little Babies' and another offers to 'Get paid $50 for 7 minutes of your time'. LinkedIn advertising is corroborated: 23+ ads, 7 company page and 16 thought leader ads by staff, one reading '9 out of 10 LinkedIn advertisers we audit fall for this simple little math problem'. Paid social is contradicted: it sells paid social and runs no social ad pixel. CRO is contradicted: it sells CRO and no testing tool was detected on its homepage. Publishing cadence: 0 of 857 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days, 38 in 365, 1 AI URL. No llms.txt, no AI crawlers blocked, and no tags detected at all on a WordPress and Gatsby house.
market:
Horus puts KlientBoost at tailwind index 2.9, band Neutral, 17:31 on the Solar Arc, dusk (Atum). Best placed for KJ1 (the click replaced by the citation, driven by AI Search / GEO). Most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle hollowed out, driven by Paid Search, Paid Social and SEO) and KJ4 (the platforms absorbing the execution layer). Best scenario fit: The Walled Oasis at 44/100. It is making P4 (supplying the inputs automation runs on), partial on P1 and P7 (some owned audience work shows), absent on P2, P6 and P8; P3 does not apply and P5 is unknown despite the pricing page in its navigation.

The Monsoon read is 51.9, band Breeze, percentile 34: migration 50.4 against displacement 53.4. The sold mix supplies 50 of the index, SEO (11) and Paid Search (11) carrying the most movable hours; the work would go 65% to South and Southeast Asia and 25% to Latin America, and automation overlaps 30%. The footprint is inferred: no hub offices, no onshore claims, mixed client type adding 3 points.
openings:
The strongest opening is the CRO contradiction: it sells CRO and landing page design, and its own homepage carries no testing tool and no tags at all. A rival selling CRO with a live testing stack on its own site can very likely (high confidence) win that comparison in front of the buyers it names. Falsifier: a later compile detecting a testing tool or a social pixel on klientboost.com closes it.

Paid social has the same shape: sold on Facebook Ads and LinkedIn Ads pages, no social pixel on the house. The book is thin: 10 of 10 clients are names without described work against a claim of 200+ case studies, and UBTECH Robotics already sits with valtech. No ads tested inside AI assistants (P8 absent) and no audited AI visibility product behind the GEO page (P1 partial): a rival with a citation share number leads with it. Displacement at 53.4 says the book does not buy mainly on price, so the pitch is proof against its own accountability language: ask for the case study behind the 63% ROI claim. The idle sitemap (0 updates in 90 days) is the symptom to raise.
watch: I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, October 2026: output or outcome pricing at a top five holdco would test an outcome agency whose own pricing model the record cannot read.

I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, late October 2026: growth below 10% flags cannibalization of the paid search lead, above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and the KJ1 tailwind.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.
I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend, rolling: the $2B milestone and pricing below $20 CPM decide whether the KJ2 tailwind arrives while its P8 stays absent.
The Google ads last shown 2026-09-21 with 39 of 49 in the last 30 days: the next compile should show whether the paid interview recruitment ad and the LinkedIn thought leader volume continue.
